classification.difficultyReason: Calculate the semiperimeter, substitute into Heron’s formula and take the positive square root, retaining exact surds.

content.prompt:
The area $A$ cm² of a triangle with side lengths $a$ cm, $b$ cm and $c$ cm is given by Heron’s formula
$$A^2=s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c),$$
where $s=\frac{a+b+c}{2}=\text{half the perimeter}$.

Find the exact areas of the triangles whose side lengths are given below.

spec.description: Unshaded scalene triangle with a low left vertex, an upper vertex towards the left and a right vertex between their heights. Ordinary source blue outlines are rendered in house black; coordinates express the schematic shape rather than numerical dimensions.
spec.mathematics: Side a joins the left and upper vertices; side b joins the upper and right vertices; side c joins the right and left vertices. No numerical dimensions or angle conditions are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: All three side labels are permanent givens.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}s&=\frac{6+8+10}{2}=12\\A^2&=12(12-6)(12-8)(12-10)\\A^2&=12\times6\times4\times2\\A^2&=576\\A&=\sqrt{576}=24\end{align*}$$
The area is $24\text{ cm}^2$; take the positive square root because area is positive.

$$\begin{align*}s&=\frac{5+12+13}{2}=15\\A^2&=15(15-5)(15-12)(15-13)\\A^2&=15\times10\times3\times2\\A^2&=900\\A&=\sqrt{900}=30\end{align*}$$
The area is $30\text{ cm}^2$; take the positive square root because area is positive.
